title: Introduction to Databases
overview: Databases are used to store, organize, and manage application data. Node.js applications commonly connect with databases to save and retrieve information.

example.title: Database Usage
example.content:
Application
 ↓
Node.js Backend
 ↓
Database
 ↓
Stored Data

title: Types of Databases
overview: Databases are mainly divided into SQL and NoSQL databases. Each type stores and manages data differently.

example.title: Database Types
example.content:
SQL:
MySQL
PostgreSQL

NoSQL:
MongoDB
Firebase

title: Connecting Node.js with Database
overview: Node.js uses database drivers or libraries to establish communication between the application and database.

title: MongoDB with Node.js
overview: MongoDB is a popular NoSQL database commonly used with Node.js applications because it stores data in JSON-like documents.

title: Using Mongoose
overview: Mongoose is an Object Data Modeling library that helps Node.js applications interact with MongoDB easily.

title: CRUD Operations
overview: CRUD operations represent the basic database actions: Create, Read, Update, and Delete data.

example.title: CRUD
example.content:
Create → Add data
Read → Get data
Update → Modify data
Delete → Remove data

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned database concepts, database types, connecting Node.js with databases, MongoDB, Mongoose, and CRUD operations.
